# Operator-Based PostgreSQL Self-Provisioning for Gen AI Studio (Branch A)

## Description

Branch A of the conditional decomposition: implemented if the go/no-go gate decides that RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization) delivers the RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the target release. This epic implements PostgreSQL-with-pgvector lifecycle management for Gen AI Studio in that operator layer, following the model-registry-operator's auto-provisioning pattern, so that a default vector store is available out-of-the-box with no manual setup. Until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where this logic can live — the upstream ogx-k8s-operator cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning — which is why this work exists only in this branch.

## Scope

- In the Gen AI Studio operator module delivered by RHAISTRAT-7164, implement self-provisioning of a PostgreSQL instance with pgvector for playground RAG, following the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL provisioning pattern (Deployment, Service, credentials secret, and related resources owned and reconciled by the operator).
- Use the existing Red Hat image `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`, which includes pgvector — no custom image build, no Konflux onboarding. Reference the image via the related-image mechanism already present in the rhods-operator CSV so disconnected installs resolve correctly.
- Provision per the scoping model decided by the go/no-go gate — per-namespace instances are the expected default, providing multi-tenant isolation.
- Apply resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted per the validation benchmark's recommendation.
- Manage the full lifecycle: creation when a playground with RAG needs a default vector store and none exists in scope, reconciliation to desired state, and cleanup when the owning resource is removed.
- Design for portability toward the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL direction (DSC-managed, RHOAI 3.6+): consume a shared connection string when one is available rather than always self-provisioning.
- Provide a rollback/disable path: the self-provisioning can be turned off (falling back to the inline-provider behavior while it remains in the distribution, or to user-provided PostgreSQL).

Out of scope: the OGX vector_io provider configuration (a separate epic consumes the provisioned connection); benchmarking (already resolved by the validation benchmark); Auto Rag (RHAISTRAT-7824).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A playground with RAG configured gets a working default vector store with zero manual provisioning or configuration of external infrastructure — PostgreSQL with pgvector is provisioned automatically and its connection details are available to the consuming configuration.
- The provisioned PostgreSQL runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX server (not an inline provider).
- Instances are scoped per the decided model, with per-namespace isolation as the default for multi-tenant environments.
- Resource requests/limits follow the benchmark-informed sizing, keeping the default store lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments.
- Lifecycle is operator-managed: reconciliation to desired state, and cleanup when the owning resource is deleted — no orphaned database resources remain.
- The image reference resolves for disconnected installs via the related-image mechanism.
- When a platform-provided shared connection string is available, the provisioning defers to it instead of self-provisioning (portability criterion).
- The provisioning can be disabled, with a documented fallback (inline provider while available, or user-provided PostgreSQL).

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning) — primary deliverable of this branch.
- AC-4 (separate process, not inline) — provisioned PostgreSQL is a distinct workload.
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation) — per the decided scoping model.
- AC-6 (lightweight, resource-constrained environments) — benchmark-informed sizing.

## Branch Metadata

- Branch: A — go/no-go outcome "RHAISTRAT-7164 lands in time; operator-based self-provisioning".
- If this outcome does not hold, this epic is removed and the plan falls back to Branch B (BFF-managed provisioning) or the bring-your-own path.

# BFF-Managed PostgreSQL Provisioning for Gen AI Studio (Branch B)

## Description

Branch B of the conditional decomposition: implemented if the go/no-go gate decides that RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization) will not deliver the RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the target release, and the team chooses to preserve the out-of-the-box experience without an operator. The gen-ai BFF provisions the default vector store directly: when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable PostgreSQL instance exists in scope, the BFF creates the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and credentials secret — mirroring how the BFF already provisions guardrails infrastructure. This path carries explicit lifecycle risk that the Staff Engineer Input flags: the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, pod-restart handling, and credential rotation need explicit design attention, and the implementation must stay portable to the platform-provided shared database expected in a later release.

## Scope

- In the gen-ai BFF, implement provisioning of a PostgreSQL-with-pgvector instance (Deployment, Service, PVC, credentials secret) when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable instance exists in the namespace, reusing the existing Red Hat image `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` (pgvector included — no custom image build, no Konflux onboarding).
- Make provisioning idempotent: detect an existing suitable instance and reuse it rather than duplicating.
- Provision per the scoping model decided by the go/no-go gate — per-namespace instances are the expected default, providing multi-tenant isolation.
- Apply resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted per the validation benchmark's recommendation.
- Design the lifecycle explicitly, since the BFF has no reconciliation loop: cleanup of the provisioned resources when the owning playground is deleted; behavior across BFF pod restarts (reconciliation-on-action rather than continuous reconciliation); database credential rotation handling.
- Design for portability toward the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL direction (DSC-managed, RHOAI 3.6+): when a shared connection string is available, the BFF must consume it rather than self-provisioning.
- Provide a rollback/disable path: BFF-managed provisioning can be turned off, falling back to user-provided PostgreSQL (bring-your-own) or to the inline-provider behavior while it remains in the distribution.

Out of scope: the OGX vector_io provider configuration (a separate epic consumes the provisioned connection); the operator-based provisioning path (the alternative branch); Auto Rag (RHAISTRAT-7824).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A playground with RAG configured gets a working default vector store with zero manual provisioning — the BFF provisions PostgreSQL with pgvector and its connection details are available to the consuming configuration.
- Provisioning is idempotent: an existing suitable instance in scope is reused; repeated configuration does not create duplicates.
- The provisioned PostgreSQL runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX server (not an inline provider).
- Instances are scoped per the decided model, with per-namespace isolation as the default for multi-tenant environments.
- Resource requests/limits follow the benchmark-informed sizing, keeping the default store lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments.
- Lifecycle behavior is designed and verified: deleting the owning playground cleans up the provisioned resources (no orphans); BFF pod restarts leave provisioned resources consistent and recoverable; credential rotation is handled or explicitly documented as out of scope with rationale.
- When a platform-provided shared connection string is available, the BFF consumes it instead of self-provisioning (portability criterion).
- The provisioning can be disabled, with a documented fallback (user-provided PostgreSQL, or inline provider while available).

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning) — primary deliverable of this branch.
- AC-4 (separate process, not inline) — provisioned PostgreSQL is a distinct workload.
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation) — per the decided scoping model.
- AC-6 (lightweight, resource-constrained environments) — benchmark-informed sizing.

## Branch Metadata

- Branch: B — go/no-go outcome "RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time; BFF-managed provisioning preserves the out-of-the-box experience".
- If this outcome does not hold, this epic is removed: the operator-based branch (A) proceeds instead, or the gate selects the bring-your-own path where no provisioning automation is built.

# Validate pgvector as the Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG

## Description

This investigation resolves whether PostgreSQL with pgvector is an adequate default vector store for Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows, ahead of committing the provisioning and configuration work. It runs the sprint 1 benchmark directed by the Staff Engineer Input: capture the current inline Milvus provider baseline, exercise representative playground RAG workloads against a pgvector-backed instance using OGX's existing remote `remote::pgvector` vector_io provider, and verify pgvector performs in the same order of magnitude as the baseline. It also produces the resource-sizing recommendation for the provisioned PostgreSQL instance. The outcome gates every downstream epic that builds on the pgvector default-store choice: if pgvector is not adequate, the default vector store selection is re-evaluated and downstream work is rewritten.

## Scope

- Stand up a PostgreSQL instance with pgvector using the existing Red Hat image (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`, which includes pgvector out of the box — no custom image build, no Konflux onboarding).
- Configure OGX with the remote pgvector vector_io provider (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) against that instance, reusing the existing remote vector store implementation — no OGX provider development is in scope.
- Capture the inline Milvus provider baseline for the same workloads (current playground RAG behavior).
- Run representative playground RAG workloads — typical usage involves small document sets; per the Staff Engineer Input, this is a development-experimentation default, not a production store: no latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) apply.
- Compare pgvector results against the inline Milvus baseline and verify same-order-of-magnitude performance; verify that flat scan (no vector index) is sufficient at typical playground document-set sizes.
- Recommend PostgreSQL resource requests/limits for the provisioned instance, starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing and adjusting based on the measured results.
- Record the comparison, the pass/fail verdict against the order-of-magnitude criterion, and the sizing recommendation in a benchmark report consumable by the provisioning and configuration work.

Out of scope (per Staff Engineer Input): latency threshold SLAs, corpus size range studies, index type selection, Auto Rag compatibility (RHAISTRAT-7824 scope), and production-scale workload validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Inline Milvus provider baseline for representative playground RAG workloads is captured and documented.
- A pgvector-backed OGX instance serves the same workloads through the remote `remote::pgvector` vector_io provider.
- The benchmark report states whether pgvector is within the same order of magnitude of the inline Milvus baseline, with the measurement methodology and raw numbers attached.
- Flat-scan (no index) sufficiency at typical playground document-set sizes is confirmed or refuted with evidence.
- A resource-sizing recommendation (requests/limits) is produced, starting from model-registry-operator PostgreSQL values and adjusted per the measurements.
- The verdict explicitly gates downstream work: a negative result triggers re-evaluation of the default vector store choice rather than silent continuation.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-2 (Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store, no loss of current capability) — validated by the benchmark comparison.
- AC-6 (default vector store lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments) — validated by the sizing recommendation.
- Strategy open questions on latency thresholds, corpus sizes, and index types — resolved here at dev-experimentation scope per Staff Engineer Input.

# Go/No-Go Gate: Provisioning Approach and Scoping Model for the Default Vector Store

## Description

This investigation produces the go/no-go gate decision the Staff Engineer Input directs the development team to define as part of sprint planning. It resolves two genuine unknowns that determine which provisioning work exists and what it does:

1. **Provisioning approach for the current release.** Operator-based self-provisioning requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio, which only exists once RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization, In Progress) delivers — a hard dependency with uncertain timing, since the upstream ogx-k8s-operator cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The bounded outcomes are: (A) RHAISTRAT-7164 lands in time — operator-based self-provisioning following the model-registry-operator pattern; (B) it does not — BFF-managed provisioning preserving the out-of-the-box experience; (C) both automation paths are rejected — bring-your-own PostgreSQL, where users manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their connection details (no provisioning automation is built; this outcome aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0).
2. **Scoping model for the default vector store.** Per namespace, per OGX server instance, or both. Per-namespace is the stated preference for isolation; the only stated driver for per-instance scoping (Auto Rag) has been moved to RHAISTRAT-7824's scope by the Staff Engineer Input, but the strategy author explicitly flagged the question as open, so it is resolved here rather than assumed.

The deliverable is a decision record consumed in sprint planning, covering the gate date and criterion against RHAISTRAT-7164's delivery, the selected provisioning path, and the scoping model. This is a coordination and governance decision, not a technical spike — it routes to a person, not to the investigation skill.

## Scope

- Track RHAISTRAT-7164 delivery status and forecast against the target release timeline; define the explicit gate date after which the fallback is selected.
- Evaluate the viability and risk of each outcome: operator-based self-provisioning (depends on the delivered operator layer), BFF-managed provisioning (lifecycle risks: the BFF is not an operator — cleanup on playground deletion, pod-restart handling, credential rotation), and bring-your-own PostgreSQL (breaking-change communication, manual configuration support).
- Decide the scoping model (per-namespace preferred; per-instance only if a within-scope consumer requires it).
- Record the decision with rationale, the gate date, and the consequences for the downstream provisioning work; communicate to stakeholders of RHAISTRAT-7474 (inline provider removal), which is blocked on this strategy.

Out of scope: implementing any provisioning path (that is the branch work selected by this decision); re-litigating the pgvector choice (resolved by the validation benchmark).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision record exists stating the gate date and the pass/fail criterion against RHAISTRAT-7164 delivery.
- The selected provisioning approach (operator-based, BFF-managed, or bring-your-own) is recorded with rationale and risk assessment.
- The scoping model (per-namespace vs per-instance vs both) is recorded with rationale; per-namespace isolation is the default unless a within-scope consumer requires otherwise.

# Enable the pgvector vector_io Provider on Gen AI Studio Playground OGXServer Instances

## Description

This epic wires Gen AI Studio playgrounds to use the default vector store: when the gen-ai BFF (odh-dashboard) creates and configures OGXServer instances for playgrounds with RAG, it enables OGX's existing remote `remote::pgvector` vector_io provider (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) and binds the PostgreSQL connection details from a secret. The provider itself already exists in the OGX distribution — per the Staff Engineer Input, the existing remote vector store implementation is largely reusable and the majority of the strategy's effort is infrastructure and provisioning, not provider integration. This epic is the configuration half: it works identically whether the PostgreSQL instance is platform-provisioned (per the selected provisioning approach) or user-provided (bring-your-own), so it proceeds independently of that decision.

## Scope

- In the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer creation/configuration path (where storage settings are currently set for playground instances), enable the remote pgvector vector_io provider via its environment-variable guard (`ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) and pass the PostgreSQL connection details from a secret.
- Support both connection sources: a platform-provisioned default vector store secret and a user-provided (bring-your-own) PostgreSQL connection — the bring-your-own path is the strategy's fallback if no provisioning automation lands, and matches OGX 1.0's configuration model where users can set connection details on the OGXServer CR spec.
- Bind the connection according to the scoping model decided by the go/no-go gate (per-namespace preferred); the binding must remain compatible with per-instance scoping if that decision changes.
- Leave OGX application storage untouched: per the Staff Engineer Input, vector storage and application storage are independent configurations — the application storage backend stays on its existing default (SQLite). No storage consolidation and no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration work.
- Add the ability to disable the default vector store configuration, falling back to the existing inline-provider behavior while it remains in the distribution (rollback path for the capability this strategy replaces, ahead of the inline-provider removal).
- Document the configuration path for users supplying their own PostgreSQL connection details, and the path from the default vector store to external/production-grade vector databases via OGX's existing remote vector_io providers (the strategy's migration-path open question, resolved at documentation level).

Out of scope: provisioning the PostgreSQL instance itself (that is the selected provisioning approach's work); OGX provider code changes; Auto Rag (RHAISTRAT-7824 scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Playground OGXServer instances created for RAG run with the remote pgvector vector_io provider enabled and connected to a PostgreSQL instance — the vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX server (not an inline provider).
- Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows (document upload, embedding, retrieval, generation) function against the default vector store with no loss of current capability, verified against the inline Milvus baseline comparison from the validation benchmark.
- The configuration works with both a platform-provisioned connection secret and a user-provided PostgreSQL connection; the documented bring-your-own path is sufficient for a user to restore RAG functionality without any provisioning automation.
- The default vector store enablement can be disabled, reverting to the existing inline-provider behavior while it remains available in the distribution.
- OGX application storage configuration is unchanged from its current default; no migration of application storage occurs.
- The documented path from the default vector store to an external vector database exists and is technically reviewed against the OGX vector_io provider configuration.
- Connection binding follows the decided scoping model and provides per-namespace isolation as the default.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box) — this epic provides the consumption path; full out-of-the-box delivery additionally requires the selected provisioning approach.
- AC-2 (Gen AI Studio playground RAG functions, no loss of capability) — end-to-end configuration and verification.
- AC-4 (default vector store runs as a separate process, not inline) — remote provider configuration.
- AC-6 (lightweight operation) — binds to the benchmark's sizing recommendation for the provisioned instance.
- Strategy open question "migration path to a production-grade vector database" — resolved as the documented external-vector-database configuration path.
- Rule 23 (replaces existing capability) — disable/revert acceptance criterion above.
